overall_summary: Crypto markets face bearish pressure today with Bitcoin ETFs recording 469 million dollars in outflows and large deposits hitting Binance that signal sell pressure. Bitcoin has reclaimed the 61,000 dollar level amid volatility but geopolitical tensions from Iran and broader risk-off flows weigh on sentiment. Traders are also watching U.S. economic data and steady Fed policy for further cues.

items.title: US Bitcoin ETFs See $469M Outflow on June 24
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of 469 million dollars on June 24 according to Farside data, with BlackRock's IBIT leading at over 239 million out. This continues a streak of recent redemptions and adds selling pressure to the market. Traders should watch these flows closely as they represent the largest institutional bid or offer for Bitcoin right now.
items.impact: Increases near-term downward pressure on Bitcoin price.

items.title: Bitcoin Reclaims $61,000 Level Amid Volatility
items.summary: Bitcoin bounced back above 61,000 dollars in the last 24 hours after testing lower levels around 60,500. The move comes as traders digest ongoing ETF outflows and whale activity. A sustained break higher could signal short-term relief, while failure risks deeper pullback toward key supports.
items.impact: Provides some stabilization but remains vulnerable to flows.

items.title: Large Bitcoin Deposit Hits Binance Signaling Sell Pressure
items.summary: Nearly 479 million dollars worth of Bitcoin flowed into Binance according to CryptoQuant, pointing to rising sell-side pressure from large holders. This on-chain move often precedes increased selling or distribution. Traders should monitor exchange inflows for signs of further downside.
items.impact: Adds to concerns over near-term supply hitting the market.

items.title: US Releases May Core PCE, GDP Revision Today
items.summary: At 8:30 AM ET, the Bureau of Economic Analysis is set to publish the final Q1 GDP estimate along with May personal income, spending, and core PCE inflation figures. Traders will watch closely for any signs of sticky inflation or softening consumer spending that could influence Fed rate path expectations. This data dump is a major driver for dollar, yields, and risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: High volatility expected across markets as data hits.

items.title: Durable Goods Orders and Jobless Claims Due
items.summary: May durable goods orders and weekly initial jobless claims are also releasing at 8:30 AM ET. Strong orders could signal resilient manufacturing while claims data offers a fresh read on labor market cooling. These add to the busy macro calendar that sets the tone for the session.
items.impact: Potential moves in equities and crypto on labor and capex signals.

items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady Last Week, Eyes No Hikes
items.summary: The FOMC kept the funds rate at 3.5-3.75 percent on June 17 and removed dovish language from its statement. Markets are now pricing zero rate hikes for the rest of the year according to recent analyst notes. Any follow-up Fed speak today could reinforce that view amid today's data.
items.impact: Supports risk-on bias if data aligns with soft landing.

items.title: US Senate Votes on Iran War Powers Resolution
items.summary: The US Senate took action on a war powers resolution related to the ongoing conflict with Iran, with reports of both approval in one vote and a later reversal blocking further measures. This comes amid continued US-Iran tensions and negotiations. Traders should watch for any impact on oil prices and broader risk sentiment from potential escalation or de-escalation signals.
items.impact: Heightens geopolitical uncertainty, pressuring risk assets like Bitcoin.

items.title: Trump Admin Seeks $70B+ for Iran War Costs
items.summary: The White House requested supplemental funding from Congress, around $70 billion or more, to cover costs of the US-Iran conflict, on top of the existing defense budget. This highlights the financial scale of the military engagement. Markets may react to signs of prolonged involvement or fiscal implications.
items.impact: Signals sustained conflict, likely weighing on equities and crypto via risk-off flows.

items.title: Iran Warns Ships on Strait of Hormuz Routes
items.summary: Iran's IRGC issued warnings that vessels must use approved routes through the Strait of Hormuz, raising fresh concerns over energy transit. This follows recent diplomatic talks and a temporary agreement framework. Any disruption risks spiking oil prices and market volatility.
items.impact: Energy supply risks could drive oil higher and hit risk assets.

items.title: US-Iran Talks Continue Amid Missile and Nuclear Issues
items.summary: Diplomatic efforts persist between the US and Iran over ballistic missiles, nuclear inspections, and the Hormuz deal, with technical talks set for Geneva. Rubio held frank discussions with Gulf allies. Progress or setbacks here could shift market risk perceptions quickly.
items.impact: Mixed signals on de-escalation may lead to choppy trading in risk assets.

items.title: Russia Shifts Air Defenses in Ukraine Conflict
items.summary: Moscow is reallocating air defenses to protect key sites like the capital and Kerch Bridge amid the Ukraine war. This tactical move comes as broader geopolitical tensions simmer. It underscores ongoing Eastern European risks that can influence global sentiment.
items.impact: Adds to layered geopolitical risks, potentially pressuring markets.

items.title: China Detains Japanese Over Rare Earth Smuggling
items.summary: Beijing detained two Japanese nationals in a dispute over alleged rare earth smuggling, escalating tensions as China opens a whistleblower hotline on critical minerals. This trade friction adds to supply chain concerns for tech and energy sectors.
items.impact: Could disrupt critical mineral flows, weighing on related industries and risk assets.
